items.headline: Wall Street’s AI doomsday trade is here: chipmakers sink while hyperscalers gain
items.summary: NVIDIA fell more than 3% during Monday trading as semiconductor stocks sold off after prominent AI leaders raised safety concerns and called for a slower development pace.

items.headline: Wall Street drops as AI worries pummel chipmakers
items.summary: Reuters reported that AMD and other chipmakers came under pressure as investors reacted to AI safety warnings, calls for slower development, and a 10-year Treasury yield briefly exceeding 5%.

items.headline: Wall Street’s AI doomsday trade is here: chipmakers sink while hyperscalers gain
items.summary: Intel declined between 5% and 6% in morning trading as the AI-safety debate pressured semiconductor and data-center infrastructure shares.

items.headline: Wall Street’s AI doomsday trade is here: chipmakers sink while hyperscalers gain
items.summary: Marvell fell between 5% and 6% in morning trading as investors reassessed the pace of AI infrastructure expansion.

items.headline: Why Wall Street is blowing off fears of an AI apocalypse
items.summary: Axios reported that the Nasdaq pared heavier losses and that hyperscaler-related shares held up better than chipmakers as investors treated the AI safety debate as a risk rather than an immediate collapse in AI spending.

items.headline: Trump and Huang unite against AI doomers in surprise on-stage call
items.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and President Trump publicly rejected calls for a broad pause in AI development, potentially supporting sentiment toward AI infrastructure companies.

items.headline: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s exclusive interview with Fortune’s Alyson Shontell
items.summary: Sam Altman discussed AI safety, the possibility of pausing development if required, and an expected delay of an OpenAI IPO until 2027.

items.headline: Markets rebound after President Trump rejects AI regulation
items.summary: Interactive Brokers reported that Trump’s rejection of calls to slow or regulate AI helped major U.S. averages recover more than half of their earlier losses during the session.
